input.quote: 14.2 Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer. Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.
input.rationale: Section 14.2 gives Vendor exclusive ownership of Deliverables created and paid for by Customer, with only a revocable, non-transferable licence limited to the Order Form term — contrary to our position that we own what we pay for. Sections 14.1 and 15.1 correctly preserve Customer Data ownership, 14.4 bars joint ownership, and 14.3/13.2 protect Vendor Technology with a perpetual paid-up licence back, so the minimal fix is to reverse the ownership direction in 14.2 with a Vendor assignment while leaving Vendor's background IP untouched.

proposal.summary: Reverse Deliverable ownership to Customer with Vendor assignment; Vendor keeps Vendor Technology under 14.3/13.2
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We own the Deliverables we commission and pay for, so we have replaced Vendor ownership plus a revocable, term-limited licence with Customer ownership and a Vendor assignment. Vendor's pre-existing Vendor Technology is unaffected and remains protected by Section 14.3 and the perpetual licence in Section 13.2.

ops.oldText: Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer. Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.
ops.newText: Customer exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer, and Vendor hereby irrevocably assigns to Customer all right, title, and interest in and to each Deliverable upon its creation. Vendor shall execute any documents Customer reasonably requests to perfect or record that assignment. Vendor may use a Deliverable only as necessary to perform the Services for Customer.
